# Layergram 2.0.4 — Mobile screen protection hardening

Layergram 2.0.4 strengthens the existing mobile screen-protection and privacy-
shield behavior without changing the Layergram message format or cryptographic
protocol.

The release now:

- applies the Android secure-window policy before Flutter content is attached
  and retains it while screen protection is active;
- hides application overlays and marks sensitive host content where the Android
  platform supports those controls;
- rejects fully and partially obscured Android touch gestures, including a
  gesture that becomes obscured after it starts;
- hardens the iOS privacy shield during screen capture and inactive states while
  restoring the previous window state afterward;
- excludes protected Flutter content from semantics, pointer input, focus, and
  tickers while the privacy shield is visible;
- documents the remaining platform, accessibility, compromised-device, and
  external-camera limits without making absolute protection claims; and
- adds Android instrumentation, iOS native, Flutter lifecycle, and privacy-
  shield regression coverage.

The documented Android source-build path was also reproduced from a fresh
public clone with Flutter 3.41.1 and Rust 1.87.0. The resulting functional APK
contained the packaged protocol-v3 backend for all three supported Android
ABIs.

Android open-source APKs remain signed with Layergram's dedicated direct-APK
certificate. Verify every download against the SHA-256 values published with
the release and on the Layergram website.
